hero.heading: Product, from the business case to the data model.
hero.lead: I'm a product manager who builds enterprise and AI products in lending, banking, and fintech.
paras: I started in business analysis — close enough to operations to see exactly where they break — and grew into product strategy and 0→1 platform work. That path is why I think in whole systems: a real product needs a clear problem, an honest business case, a clean domain model, an architecture engineering can build, an experience users actually adopt, and a commercial model that holds up. I'm comfortable owning all of it.

Lately my focus is AI-native products — where the hard part isn't the model, it's framing the use case, designing for trust, evaluating honestly, and pricing the value. I care about products that ship and move a number, not artifacts that sit in a deck.

timeline.p: Leading 0→1 AI products across collections and contract intelligence — owning discovery, domain modeling, AI design, and go-to-market.
Rebuilt loan origination as a configurable platform; shipped collections and customer-experience products across web and mobile.
Owned mobile and internet banking experiences — engagement, onboarding, and servicing journeys for retail customers.
Bridged operations and engineering on core banking and payments — where I learned to model a domain before designing a screen.

principles.p: Get the objects and lifecycle right and the screens, data, and AI fall into place. Get them wrong and nothing else saves you.

principles.h4: Earn the right to the next feature
principles.p: Lead with the painkiller, prove value, then expand. Trust compounds; scope creep doesn't.

principles.h4: AI is a product decision, not a model choice
principles.p: Use case, trust, evaluation, guardrails, and cost matter more than which LLM is trending this quarter.
A north-star metric and an honest unit economics model keep a product honest — and a roadmap defensible.

cta.heading: Building something hard? I'd like to hear about it.
